sections.title: Leaves and growth
sections.text: Rheum rhabarbarum is a robust, rhizomatous perennial about 1–1.5 m tall and similarly broad. Large basal, heart-shaped leaves have wavy edges and long, fleshy stalks; the flower stem rises above the foliage.

sections.title: Flowers and seeds
sections.text: A tall, branched panicle bears many tiny greenish-white to yellowish flowers, followed by dry, winged, triangular seeds.

sections.title: Food and toxicity
sections.text: In culinary rhubarb, the tart leaf stalks (petioles) are eaten, usually cooked; the leaf blades must be discarded because of their oxalic acid content. This botanical species is among the ancestry of cultivated rhubarb, so the familiar food use applies chiefly to selected culinary cultivars.
